paragraphs: Klir sells compliance and operations software built for drinking water and wastewater utilities. The argument for it is that administration and paperwork take up more than half the working time of utility scientists, engineers and operators. The platform holds that work as centralized, accessible data in one place.

On the drinking water side it manages SDWA permit adherence from start to finish. For wastewater it manages NPDES permit adherence. Pretreatment teams track industrial user details, permits and data. Staff reach it anywhere through a cloud platform with mobile inspections and field data entry. It is described as configurable and compatible with a Microsoft Azure stack alongside LIMS, GIS and SCADA.

Co-founders David Lynch and Elaine Kelly met while working with European drinking water and wastewater utilities and regulators. The company says large water and wastewater organizations in the United States, Canada and Australia now use it to centralize and automate compliance reporting. The team has grown past 60 people across the United States, Canada, Brazil and Ireland. The company lists SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 and NIST compliance, and sells directly, through the Microsoft Azure Marketplace or on cooperative contracts.
